title: Will one more control help?
hook: An extra column may help prediction while changing the causal comparison.

knows: arithmetic means, rates and simple plotted values
doesNotKnow: adding every available variable can increase bias rather than remove it.

misconception: Treating kitchen-sink regression as valid without checking the stated model, denominators or causal assumptions.
objective: adding every available variable can increase bias rather than remove it.
keyState: Both finite cases completed; their computed summaries retained.

claims.text: Let independent fair binary T,U generate Y=2T+U and the proposed control M=T+U. Comparing T=1 and T=0 within M=1 gives what outcome difference?

claims.text: Controlling M=1 retains difference 1; the unadjusted randomized comparison retains 2. At fixed M, treated units must have lower U, so the new comparison changes more than T.

claims.text: M is a shared effect of treatment and the outcome’s other cause. More controls can create bias rather than remove it. Choose controls from the causal question and graph, not simply from every available column.

claims.text: Should every available post-treatment variable automatically enter a causal adjustment set? Post-treatment variables may be mediators or colliders, changing the estimand or introducing bias.
